name: ODDLYIELD
description: ODDLYIELD returns the yield to maturity for a bond with an irregular last coupon period.
tldr: Calculates the yield of a security with an odd last coupon period.
syntax: (settlement, maturity, last_interest, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])

parameters.name: last_interest
parameters.description: Date of the last coupon payment before settlement.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.description: Yield of a bond with an odd last coupon period
basicExample.explanation: Calculates the yield for a bond priced at $95 with an irregular last coupon period.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 is common for Treasury bonds.

howItWorks: ODDLYIELD solves for the yield that equates the present value of the bond's cash flows, including the irregular last coupon, to the purchase price.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: All dates must be valid Excel dates.
Last interest date must be before maturity.

commonErrors.fix: Verify all inputs and date order.
Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ODDLYIELD works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between ODDLYIELD and YIELD?
faq.answer: ODDLYIELD is for bonds with an irregular last coupon period. YIELD is for standard bonds.

faq.question: When is ODDLYIELD used?
faq.answer: It is used for bonds that mature on an off-cycle date.
